description: This course covers software project management methodologies including Agile (Scrum, Kanban), Waterfall, and Spiral models; project planning using Microsoft Project and Jira; risk management with FMEA and SWOT analysis; cost estimation using COCOMO and function point analysis; quality assurance with ISO 9001 and CMMI standards; team management using Scrum roles (Product Owner, Scrum Master); requirement gathering with UML use cases; and project closure with lessons learned and post-mortem reviews. Students will learn to apply these tools and techniques to real-world software projects.

clos.text: Define the key phases of the software development lifecycle (SDLC) and explain how they align with project management methodologies such as Scrum, Waterfall, and Spiral.
Describe the components of a project charter and create a work breakdown structure (WBS) using Microsoft Project for a sample software project.
Explain the principles of risk management in software projects and apply FMEA and SWOT analysis to identify and mitigate potential project risks.
Apply cost estimation techniques such as COCOMO and function point analysis to calculate project costs and schedule for a given software project.
Implement a project management plan using Jira and Scrum practices, including sprint planning, daily standups, and retrospectives for a simulated software development team.

labs: Create a project schedule using Microsoft Project
Perform cost estimation using COCOMO model
Conduct risk assessment using SWOT analysis
Evaluate a software project against ISO 9001 standards
Document software requirements using UML use cases
Simulate a sprint planning session using Jira
Perform earned value analysis on a simulated project
Track project changes using Git version control
Conduct a post-mortem review for a software project
Integrate Jira and Confluence for project documentation

topics: Case Studies in Software Project Management

labs: Present final project management plan to peers
